title: Correctness: KEY_GENERATE does not zeroize inbuf
description: Trigger: open fd, write() sensitive bytes (e.g. a key the caller was going to import but abandoned), then call CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_KEY_GENERATE. ioctl_key_generate (fd.c ~line 1591) never calls inbuf_clear(). Bad outcome: the accumulated inbuf bytes -- which may be sensitive key material -- remain in kernel heap for the entire lifetime of the KEY fd, until close(). ioctl_key_import correctly calls inbuf_clear() at line 1515 regardless of success/failure. KEY_GENERATE has no equivalent. This is a FIPS 140-3 zeroization violation: sensitive material must be destroyed as soon as it is no longer needed, not deferred to fd close. Fix: call inbuf_clear(state) immediately after key_generate succeeds (before setting fd_type).
